findings: Exercise as printed on PDF 246-250 (printed pages 243-247): 10 MCQs, 9 short answer, 9 constructed response, 6 comprehensive questions and 12 numerical problems (the last two printed as 7.11 and 7.12), each solved in English and Roman Urdu (MCQs as keyed checkpoints, the rest as self-checks with model answers; numericals worked step by step). Drafts for the academic review.
The book prints no MCQ key; keys worked out from the chapter: 10.1 d, 10.2 b, 10.3 b, 10.4 c, 10.5 a, 10.6 c, 10.7 c, 10.8 b, 10.9 c, 10.10 d.
Numerical 10.3: printed answer 0.54 V is wrong (it is the emf for the whole flux vanishing); turning through 30° gives 0.072 V. Book correction box added.

Numerical 10.9: printed positive end of rod L₁ is a; by F = q v × B (v along +y, B along +z, force along +x) the positive end is b as drawn. Book correction box added. Magnitudes (0.75 V, 0, 0) agree.

Numericals 7.11 and 7.12 keep their printed numbers (numbering slip, not boxed; owner rule 2026-11-13); the × sign missing in 7.11 ('4.96 10⁴') is written silently. Numerical 10.7: worked value 11.2 cm vs printed 11.16 cm (rounding only).

The scan is low resolution (595 × 770 px page images); small exponents in numericals 10.2 (answer), 10.6 (answer), 10.7 (V), 10.8 (v and answer) and 7.11 (v, answer) are not legible. They were written as the values consistent with the printed mantissas and answers (V = 6 × 10⁵ V gives 11.16 cm; v = 10⁷ m s⁻¹ gives 2.46 × 10⁻¹ m; 4.96 × 10⁴ × 0.114 = 5.65 × 10³). Worked answers 10.2 = 4.1 × 10⁻¹² N and 10.6 = 1.75 × 10⁻² V; the reviewer should confirm the printed exponents against the paper book.
Short 10.4 asks for the pole at 'the left end' of a vertical solenoid; answered as the end facing the magnet (south pole, since the magnet's S pole enters). Short 10.6 assumes equal charges.

Answers beyond the chapter: CRQ 10.9 (magnetic shielding with a soft-iron box; the chapter covers only electric shielding in Ch. 9), CRQ 10.2 (jumping ring, an application of Lenz's law not described in the chapter) and the Wazahat on the helical path in numerical 10.8.
